Crypto asset manager 21Shares said Bitcoin selling pressure has weakened, with its Seller Exhaustion Constant falling to approximately 0.007, placing it in the bottom 0.3% of readings since 2010.

The Details:

•	Historical rarity: The current reading represents only the 11th time the indicator has reached this level in Bitcoin’s history.

•	Past performance: In all 11 prior episodes, Bitcoin traded higher one year later, recording a median gain of 155%.

•	Short-term risk: 21Shares noted that past instances experienced additional near-term downside before resolving higher.

•	Bottom caveat: The asset manager cautioned that the low reading does not necessarily mark an immediate price bottom.

Nvidia ($NVDA) is in discussions to invest in artificial intelligence startup Perplexity as part of a funding round valuing the company at over $30 billion.

The Details:

•	Valuation growth: The prospective funding round marks a 50% valuation increase from Perplexity’s previous $20 billion valuation finalized last year.

•	Revenue expansion: Perplexity’s annualized revenue climbed past $750 million from under $250 million earlier this year, boosted by its Perplexity Computer agent.

•	Infrastructure agreements: Perplexity previously signed a $750 million Azure cloud computing agreement with Microsoft ($MSFT).

•	Public listing: Chief Executive Aravind Srinivas stated the company plans to pursue an initial public offering in 2028.

The U.S. reportedly offered Iran a deal to halt the siege and lift sanctions in exchange for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and ending proxy attacks, according to Al Arabiya. Axios also reports that Rubio told several foreign counterparts the U.S. does not plan new strikes on Iran for now, with pressure shifting toward the naval blockade and new sanctions campaign instead. Crude Oil fell 4% and the 10-year treasury bond fell from 4.72% to 4.62%.

Alphabet’s ($GOOGL) Google hired Thinking Machines Lab co-founder and former OpenAI executive Barret Zoph as vice president of research to advance Gemini development.

The Details:

•	Google appointment: Google hired Zoph as vice president of research to bring reinforcement learning and post-training expertise to Gemini.

•	OpenAI tenure: Zoph previously led commercial AI enterprise product efforts at OpenAI after leaving Thinking Machines earlier this year.

•	Startup exit: Zoph left Thinking Machines in January alongside Luke Metz and Sam Schoenholz following a dispute with CEO Mira Murati.

•	Startup focus: Thinking Machines develops AI systems designed to work alongside humans rather than operate fully autonomously.

Anthropic has reportedly signed a $35 billion cloud-computing agreement with Nvidia-backed Lambda for capacity at a Texas data center developed by Hut 8, according to people familiar with the transaction.

The Details:

•	Structure: Nvidia reportedly holds the data-center lease after securing capacity from Hut 8; Lambda would install Nvidia chips at the Nueces County, Texas site.

•	Hut 8 campus: Hut 8 disclosed 15-year leases for the full 700-megawatt campus from an unnamed tenant and described the planned facility as a $20 billion Nvidia-chip project.

•	Supply expansion: The arrangement follows Anthropic’s reported $45 billion agreement with Nvidia-backed Nscale earlier this month for West Virginia capacity.

$DELL DELL delivered another huge beat and raise, reporting record quarterly revenue of $47.0B versus $44.9B expected, up 58% YoY. Adjusted EPS came in at $7.04 versus $4.91 expected, up 203% YoY from $2.32. AI server revenue reached $16.4B, roughly doubling YoY, while Dell booked a massive $60.9B of AI server orders during the quarter. AI backlog surged to a record $95B, up from $51.3B last quarter, one of the biggest numbers in the report. Infrastructure also remained strong, with traditional servers and networking revenue up 122% YoY to $10.5B and storage revenue up 26% to $4.9B.
